knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE,

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(brms)
library(cmdstanr)
library(mice)
library(posterior)
library(bayesplot)

# Helper function to save plots
save_plot <- function(plot, filename, width = 9, height = 6) {
  ggsave(
    filename = file.path('../figures/cmdstan_hmc', filename),
    plot = plot,
    width = width,
    height = height,
    dpi = 300
  )
}

hmc_model <- read_rds('../data/models/hmc_model.rds')
```

### Convergence diagnostics

These functions help identify how well our HMC markov chains explored the posterior distribution. Essentially verifies if the markov chains reached our target distributions. This is helpful to identify issues in our chosen amount of iterations, number of chains, sampling efficiency-our model fit parameters. May also be useful to adjust our priors.

Get Rhat and effective sample size
```{r}
# Extract posterior draws
draws <- as_draws_array(hmc_model)

# Calculate convergence statistics
convergence <- summarise_draws(
  draws,
  mean,
  sd,
  rhat,
  ess_bulk,
  ess_tail,
  mcse_mean
)

# Save convergence statistics
write_csv(convergence,
          '../figures/cmdstan_hmc/convergence_statistics.csv')
```

Divergent transitions
```{r}
# Check the number of divergent transitions
np <- nuts_params(hmc_model)

divergences <- np |>
  filter(Parameter == "divergent__") |>
  summarise(
    total_divergences = sum(Value),
    total_iterations = n(),
    divergence_rate = total_divergences / total_iterations
  )

print(divergences)
```

Trace plots for parameters (Important)
```{r}
# variables(hmc_model)
p_trace <- mcmc_trace(
  draws,
  pars = c(
    "b_Intercept",

    "b_WSPM_z",

save_plot(p_trace, "trace_plots.png")
```

```{r}

)

save_plot(p_density, "mc_density_overlays.png")
```

### Posterior Distribution Plots

This visualizes our posterior distributions and 95% credible intervals for the regression coefficients and variance parameters.

Regression Coefficients
```{r}
p_coefficients <- mcmc_areas(
  draws,
  pars = c(
    "b_TEMP_z",
    "b_DEWP_z",
    "b_WSPM_z"
  ),
  prob = 0.95
) +
  labs(title = "Posterior Distributions of Regression Coefficients") +
  theme_minimal()

save_plot(
  p_coefficients,
  "regression_coefficients.png",
  width = 10,
  height = 6
)
```

Residual and station standard deviation
```{r}
p_hyperparameters <- mcmc_areas(
  draws,
  pars = c(
    "sd_station__Intercept",
    "sigma"
  ),
  prob = 0.95
) +
  labs(title = "Posterior Distributions of Model Parameters") +
  theme_minimal()

save_plot(
  p_hyperparameters,
  "hierarchical_parameters.png",
  width = 10,
  height = 6
)
```

Station baseline distributions
```{r}
# Extract random intercept posterior draws
station_effects <- ranef(
  hmc_model,
  summary = FALSE
)$station

# Extract population intercept
posterior_draws <- as_draws_df(hmc_model)

station_names <- dimnames(station_effects)[[2]]

# Calculate station-specific baselines
station_baselines <- map_dfr(
  seq_along(station_names),
  function(j) {
    tibble(
      station = station_names[j],
      baseline = posterior_draws$b_Intercept +
        station_effects[, j, "Intercept"]
    )
  }
)

# Plot station baseline distributions
p_station <- ggplot(
  station_baselines,
  aes(x = baseline, fill = station)
) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.35) +
  labs(
    title = "Posterior Distributions of Station Baselines",
    x = "Standardized log-PM2.5",
    y = "Posterior density",
    fill = "Station"
  ) +
   scale_fill_manual(
     values = c("Tiantan" = "darkblue",
                "Wanliu" = "#FF8C00",
                "Wanshouxigong" = "#88E788")) +
  theme_minimal()

save_plot(
  p_station,
  "station_baselines.png",
  width = 10,
  height = 6
)
```


### Posterior Predictive Checks

These test how well our fitted model represents the observed data, by comparing/overlaying the observed to simulated datasets, which is drawn from our HMC estimated posterior distributions.

Posterior predictive check of target population parameter PM2.5
```{r}
# Simulate replicated datasets from the model and compare them with the observed data.

# We simulate 200 replicated datasets
set.seed(123)

yrep <- posterior_predict(
  hmc_model,
  ndraws = 200
)

# Compare observed and replicated distributions
p_ppc <- ppc_dens_overlay(
  y = imp$PM25_z,
  yrep = yrep[1:100, ]
) +
  labs(
    title = "Posterior Predictive Check",
    x = "Standardized log-PM2.5",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

save_plot(
  p_ppc,
  "posterior_predictive.png",
  width = 10,
  height = 7
)
```

PPC by station
```{r}
stations <- unique(imp$station)

p_ppc_station <- map(
  stations,
  function(s) {

    idx <- which(imp$station == s)

    ppc_dens_overlay(
      y = imp$PM25_z[idx],
      yrep = yrep[1:100, idx, drop = FALSE]
    ) +
      labs(
        title = s,
        x = "Standardized log-PM2.5",
        y = "Density"
      ) +
      theme_minimal()
  }
) |>
  patchwork::wrap_plots(ncol = 3) +
  patchwork::plot_annotation(
    title = "Posterior Predictive Checks by Station"
  )

save_plot(
  p_ppc_station,
  "ppc_by_station.png",
  width = 15,
  height = 6
)
```

### Residuals Diagnostic

To test how well our model fits to the data (it doesnt)

Residuals vs. Fitted
```{r}
# Generate posterior expected values
epred <- posterior_epred(
  hmc_model,
  ndraws = 500
)

# Calculate posterior median fitted values
fitted_values <- apply(epred, 2, median)

# Construct residual dataset
residual_data <- imp |>
  mutate(
    fitted = fitted_values,
    residual = PM25_z - fitted
  )

# Plot residuals
p_residual <- ggplot(
  residual_data,
  aes(x = fitted, y = residual)
) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "loess",
    se = TRUE
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Residuals vs Fitted Values",
    x = "Posterior Median Fitted Values",
    y = "Residuals"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

save_plot(
  p_residual,
  "residuals_vs_fitted.png"
)
```
